title: Step 5 - an in-memory store guarded by a mutex
intro: `Store` keeps bookmarks in memory and picks their ids.
An HTTP server runs each request in its own goroutine,
so `Add` may run twice at once. Both could read the same
length and hand out the same id. `sync.Mutex` lets one
goroutine at a time in: `Lock`, then `defer Unlock` so
every return lets go. `List` returns a copy, so callers
never read the slice while it is being changed.
`Get` returns `(Bookmark, bool)`, the comma-ok form, like
reading a map: `b, ok := s.Get(id)`. The bool says
whether it was found, so the zero `Bookmark` is never
The zero `Store` is ready to use: no constructor needed.
